title: When the Inheritance Wakes Again
premise: True-crime podcaster Astrid Sandoval inherits the estate of Elowen Marsh, a woman who vanished in 1974, and discovers Elowen's diary contains entries written years after her disappearance. Following the diary's clues to a coastal village preparing its annual anniversary dinner for the missing, Astrid uncovers that the 'dead' witness—Elowen's sister Marguerite—has been living hidden under another identity, protected by a pact of silence among the townsfolk who helped her flee an abusive husband they believed she'd killed. As the anniversary dinner approaches, Astrid must choose between exposing the truth that will close their career-defining case and protecting the woman whose testimony could destroy half the town; in the end, Astrid records one final episode telling only half the story, letting Elowen's diary speak for itself while Marguerite finally raises her glass at the dinner, seen by no one but Astrid.
about_author: Lena Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unsolved case files in northern coastal towns before turning to fiction. They write mysteries obsessed with paper trails, family silences, and the things inheritances refuse to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Bequest
chapters.summary: Astrid Sandoval receives notice of an inheritance from Elowen Marsh, a 1974 missing person whose cold case anchored their podcast's first season. Arriving at the decaying Marsh house on the coast, they find the bequest conditional: live there through the anniversary dinner, or lose everything. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Sorting Elowen's belongings, Astrid discovers the diary continues three years past the disappearance date—the final entry naming a witness: 'M. knows everything.' The handwriting matches Elowen's exactly. Astrid's producer warns them off, sensing obsession. POV: Astrid, with diary excerpts interleaved. Emotional beat: professional thrill giving way to genuine dread.

chapters.title: The Town That Toasts a Ghost
chapters.summary: In the village of Greywater Point, Astrid interviews locals about the anniversary dinner tradition honoring Elowen. Everyone performs grief, but innkeeper Cora Hale flinches when 'Marguerite' is mentioned. An old fisherman mutters that some people are mourned so they can live. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the dawning sense of a town-wide performance.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid finds hidden letters between Elowen and her sister Marguerite revealing Elowen's husband Daniel was violent, and that Elowen planned to disappear—but the letters stop mid-sentence. At night, someone enters the house and moves nothing except the diary. POV: Astrid, with a brief unsettling interlude from an unnamed watcher. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into paranoia.

chapters.title: Daniel's Grave Is Empty
chapters.summary: Astrid exhumes the record trail: Daniel Marsh was declared dead the same week Elowen vanished, yet no body was ever verified. The town's beloved founding patriarch may have been buried as fiction. Cora warns Astrid to leave before the dinner. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the case turning personal and dangerous.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing decades of town photos, Astrid spots the same gray-eyed woman recurring under different names—always at the edge of frames, always after dark. A retired postmistress recognizes her and goes silent forever when her cottage burns that night. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: guilt over collateral damage, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: On the eve of the dinner, Astrid confronts Cora, who confesses the pact: the town helped Marguerite fake both deaths to escape Daniel, and Elowen's diary was left deliberately as insurance—a message meant to be found only if Marguerite stopped hiding. Someone has been checking it yearly. POV: Astrid and Cora alternating. Emotional beat: compassion colliding with duty.

chapters.title: The Glass Raised
chapters.summary: At the anniversary dinner, Astrid watches the toast and sees her: Marguerite, old and unafraid, raising her glass to her sister. But Daniel's grandson, armed with Astrid's published research, has come to reclaim the Marsh name—and he's brought a lawyer and questions. POV: Astrid amid the crowd. Emotional beat: climax tension, the past arriving at the table.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Cornered in the Marsh house, Marguerite tells Astrid everything: Elowen didn't vanish—she died helping Marguerite escape, and the diary's later entries are Marguerite's, written in her sister's hand to keep the insurance alive. Daniel's grandson demands silence or ruin. POV: Marguerite's confession framing Astrid's decision. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into understanding.

chapters.title: Half the Story
chapters.summary: Astrid releases a final episode narrating only what the dead can safely tell: Elowen's courage, the town's complicity in mercy, no names beyond the grave. The inheritance passes to Astrid, who keeps the house as an archive for silenced women. At next year's dinner, two glasses are raised. POV: Astrid closing the circle. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—love chosen over duty.
